Nine hundred hours in, and I’m still coming back for more. Dead by Daylight is one of the most unique multiplayer games out there: a tense 4v1 game of cat and mouse where every match plays out differently. Whether you’re a survivor sweating through a last generator or a killer hunting down the final survivor, the adrenaline never gets old.

What it does best:

Two completely different experiences. Survivor is all stealth, teamwork, and clutch escapes. Killer is about pressure, mind games, and map control. Switching sides keeps the game fresh.
Huge variety. With dozens of killers, survivors, perks, add-ons, and maps, there’s always a new build to try. No two trials feel quite the same.
Licensed chapters. Horror icons and original characters sit side by side, and each new chapter brings new powers, perks, and playstyles.
Skill ceiling. Looping, mind-gaming, tracking, and macro decisions take real time to master. After hundreds of hours I’m still learning new tricks.
Best with friends. A coordinated survivor squad or a good group in voice chat is where the game really shines.

What could be better:

Matchmaking and balance can be hit or miss, and some matches just aren’t fun.
The learning curve is steep for new players, and the first few hours can be rough.
Some DLC and cosmetics are pricey, though the game is fully playable without all of them.
Toxic players exist, as in most competitive games.

Dead by Daylight isn’t perfect, but it delivers something no other game quite matches. The thrill of a close escape, or of a hard-earned 4k, is why I’ve sunk this much time into it. If you like horror, tension, and a challenge that keeps rewarding you the more you learn, give it a try. Just don’t be surprised when you look up and see your playtime in the hundreds.

I initially quit this game back around 2020. I used to have so much fun in this game with friends, but it quickly became a toxic experience. I have nothing especially unique to say about this game, but I just want to scream into the void about how unpleasant this community is. I've played most major mobas, many competitive shooters, and lots of other online games and this by far has the most toxic player base. It's genuinely impressive how insufferable people can be in a game with next to no communication options. If you are solo queue, then you always have 4 enemies, regardless if you play killer or survivor. People are hateful, non co-operative, and will do everything to make the experience worse for everyone else.

The core gameplay isn't especially worth the pain. Frankly, I'm confused why I managed to get back into this 6 years later. Idk man, there's some fun to be had but I whole-heartedly cannot recommend this game to new players. The community is toxic and the devs are incompetent at their job. Balancing is awful and I don't mean that in an op way, I mean so many killers just feel non-viable especially against a bully stack. I year to be silly or to have a chill experience. There is rarely such an option. I see the same killers and the same small pool of meta perks over and over again. Rarely do I see someone trying to have fun or experiment in an interesting way.

DBD is an old friend that I want to rekindle a friendship with, but they make it really hard to see what I ever saw in them.

This reccomendation depends entirely on how much you hate your life and how much you're willing to dump into this game. Overall. Not a reccomendation. It's addicting at times i agree but. the devs kinda ruin it. They're incredibely out of touch with their own game. Tying a charity goal behind one sides objectives of an assymetric party game is only the latest, yet vilest, example of the devs seemingly only furthering the hate between Killer and Survivor players instead of trying to fix it. Playing killer as a casual is a pain in the ass. Now for me this is less of an issue, my hours are nothing compared to some but i can pretty consistently beat the 4 man high hour squads. there in lies the problem for me. It's a double edged blade SWF's. On the one hand, i can understand it. Playing the party game with buddies is obviously way more fun. But it also kinda hinders the balance of the game. A good 4 man has no need for any real Aura reading perks, as just calling out the killer's location is often more than enough to just straight up avoid chases. Then when you finally do get in one there's hundreds of filler pallets everywhere making it impossible to really outplay them as they can just drop and go to the next loop. Now i concede, there might be a skill issue in there. But my point is that this game is only really fun if you've devoted your life to playing it. It's hard and borderline impossible to get into. The balancing is just a joke. There's a few used "meta" perks and using any other ones will have you being called slurs, doxxed, threatened with your life or all of the above. The Devs seemingly play a whole different game than the rest of us. And above all of that. If you're a horror fan like me. This game will be real expensive for you. All the fun, iconic killers and survivors from your favorite movie or game are locked behind real paywalls. their perks are unlockable for free (if you're really lucky with the shrine which can take genuine months) but if you want to play as say Springtrap, Dracula, Leon Kennedy, ... It will cost you 5 Euro per, if not on sale. And there are a LOT of character locked behind this paywall. In general, untill by some intervention of God himself the devs do a complete 180 on this game. Stay away. (and if you do get this game, do yourself a favor and put EVERYTHING on private. You WILL be called slurs and worse. This community is no joke, and i'm a LoL player, the single WORST community i've ever had the displeasure of interacting with)

I have over 3k hours on playstation and a few hundred on pc. im a survivor main. i love to play killer but i just find survivor more appealing. no specific reason i just enjoy playing with a team. 

This game is far beyond it's prime. If you are looking for a good old nostalgia boner you might get a solid 10 or 15 hours of fun out of it before you realize how shite the game has become. 

The main reason I wanted to write this review is for people coming from the golden age of the game to what it is now. If you have not played in a few years do not expect anything great to come from the development. This game was once a fun horror game. All genuine horror aspects are no longer apparent. The scary killers are much less common, and have more so been replaced with soulless, boring, skill-less, lame and dreary killers. there genuinely has not been a fun killer since 2020. (maybe 2024 if you enjoy the unknown he is actually some what interesting.) 

This game is not balanced what so ever and still remains one of the most jank games I come back to revisit. you will find this after the first few matches. 

To new players I would still recommend trying this game out. maybe if you are playing as survivor you may get some of the fun to play against OG killers. but as a solo survivor , YOU WILL NOT HAVE A GOOD TIME. That is another big flaw this game has. solo queing as a survivor you will get paired with literal AI and some of the most braindead people imaginable. good luck. 

to OG players, there is still rarely you will get paired up with OG killers and have an actual fun game. The newer maps that are not very scary are pretty miserable to play on and make it feel as far away from a horror game as possible. you can still have fun here and there but its definitely not gaurunteed and will leave you feeling empty and wanting more.

The game has lost the plot. it is no longer a horror game. i dont even know what the hell it is. This is my final conclusion. I still have a love and passion for this game. If I had a billion dollars I would buy this useless company out and completely rebrand to what it once was. If i got my buddies on we will hop on for a while before getting bored of playing against the ghoul for the 26th game in a row. good luck to the newbies and the OGs trying this game out again. I can only hope it will return to the way it once was.

For some reason, they constantly try to make life easier for survivors, while treating killer players as if they don't want them in the game at all. They still can't decide what kind of game they’re making: a casual party game or a serious competitive PvP title. This leads to the introduction of contradictory changes.
